stem.en: The main aim of the economic policies of the colonial government in India was to:

options.en: raise the standard of living of Indians
protect and promote the economic interests of Britain

explanation.en: NCERT stresses that colonial policies served Britain's economic interests rather than India's development.

stem.en: Whose estimates of national income during the colonial period are considered very significant?

explanation.en: Among the estimators, V.K.R.V. Rao's estimates are regarded as very significant.

stem.en: During the first half of the twentieth century, the growth of aggregate real output in India was:

options.en: less than 2 per cent a year

explanation.en: NCERT notes growth of aggregate real output below 2 per cent and per capita output growth of only about half a per cent.

stem.en: Under colonial rule India mainly became a:

options.en: net importer of food grains only
supplier of raw materials and a market for British finished goods

explanation.en: The colonial economy exported primary products and imported British manufactures.

stem.en: Most national income estimates of the colonial period were inconsistent and inaccurate mainly because:

options.en: there was no agriculture to measure
the British made no sincere attempt to measure national and per capita income

explanation.en: NCERT notes that the colonial government did not make any sincere attempt to measure national and per capita income.

stem.en: The zamindari system was introduced mainly in the:

explanation.en: The zamindari (permanent settlement) system was implemented in the then Bengal Presidency.

stem.en: The main cause of stagnation in colonial agriculture was:

options.en: the system of land settlement introduced by the colonial government

explanation.en: NCERT names the land settlement systems, especially zamindari, as the main cause.

stem.en: Commercialisation of agriculture under colonial rule meant:

options.en: growing cash crops such as indigo, jute and cotton instead of food crops
selling all food grains to the government

explanation.en: Farmers shifted to commercial crops that supplied British industries.

stem.en: After the partition of 1947, a large part of the jute-producing area went to:

explanation.en: Partition sent much of the jute-growing area to East Pakistan (now Bangladesh), hurting India's jute industry.

stem.en: According to the passage, roughly what share of India's workforce depended on agriculture on the eve of independence?

explanation.en: Note the difference: 85% lived in villages, while 70–75% of people depended on agriculture.

passage.en: A history teacher shows a table of estimates for colonial India. Between 1900 and 1947 the growth of aggregate real output was less than 2 per cent a year, and per capita output grew by only about half a per cent a year. Nearly 85 per cent of the people lived in villages and 70–75 per cent depended on agriculture. Literacy was below 16 per cent, and female literacy was only about 7 per cent. Life expectancy was about 32 years.

stem.en: TISCO was incorporated in:

explanation.en: The Tata Iron and Steel Company was incorporated in 1907.

stem.en: Cotton textile mills in colonial India were concentrated mainly in:

explanation.en: Cotton mills, mostly Indian-owned, came up in the western parts of the country.

stem.en: The jute mills of colonial India were located mainly in Bengal and were dominated by:

explanation.en: NCERT notes jute mills in Bengal were dominated by foreigners.

stem.en: Which of the following was NOT a feature of colonial industrial growth?

options.en: A strong base of capital goods industries

explanation.en: There was hardly any capital goods industry in colonial India.

stem.en:
Assertion (A): The decline of Indian handicraft industries created massive unemployment in colonial India.
Reason (R): Cheap machine-made goods from Britain replaced Indian handicraft products in domestic and foreign markets.

options.en: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

explanation.en: Both are true. Competition from cheap British manufactures (with discriminatory tariffs) destroyed handicrafts, which caused unemployment, so R explains A.

stem.en: The experience of the weaver family is an example of:

explanation.en: The collapse of traditional handicrafts without replacement by modern industry is de-industrialisation.

passage.en: In the nineteenth century a weaver family in Murshidabad made fine cotton and silk cloth that sold in markets across Asia and Europe. After the British began exporting raw cotton from India and selling cheap machine-made cloth from Lancashire in Indian markets, the family's sales fell. Import duties on Indian cloth in Britain were high, while British goods entered India almost duty-free. By the end of the century the family had left weaving and become agricultural labourers.

stem.en: Which colonial policy in the passage most directly hurt the weavers?

options.en: A discriminatory tariff policy: high duties on Indian goods in Britain, duty-free entry of British goods into India

explanation.en: The passage describes discriminatory tariffs that made Indian cloth expensive abroad and British cloth cheap in India.

passage.en: In the nineteenth century a weaver family in Murshidabad made fine cotton and silk cloth that sold in markets across Asia and Europe. After the British began exporting raw cotton from India and selling cheap machine-made cloth from Lancashire in Indian markets, the family's sales fell. Import duties on Indian cloth in Britain were high, while British goods entered India almost duty-free. By the end of the century the family had left weaving and become agricultural labourers.

stem.en: Under colonial rule, more than half of India's foreign trade was with:

explanation.en: Britain maintained a monopolistic control over India's exports and imports.

stem.en: The Suez Canal, which made trade between Britain and India cheaper and faster, was opened in:

explanation.en: The Suez Canal opened in 1869 and became a highway for British goods.

stem.en: Which of these was a typical import of colonial India?

options.en: Cotton, silk and woollen clothes from British factories

explanation.en: India imported finished consumer goods and exported raw materials such as jute, indigo and raw silk.

stem.en: The export surplus of colonial India was mainly used for:

options.en: importing gold and silver into India
paying for the colonial government's expenses, war expenses and invisible imports

explanation.en: This outflow is the drain of Indian wealth.

stem.en:
Assertion (A): Colonial India had a large export surplus in its foreign trade.
Reason (R): The export surplus brought a large flow of gold and silver into India.

options.en: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

explanation.en: A is true. R is false: the surplus was used to meet British administrative and war expenses and invisible imports, so no gold or silver flowed in.

stem.en: The first official census in British India was conducted in:

explanation.en: The first census was undertaken in 1881.

stem.en: Which year is known as the "year of the great divide" in India's demographic history?

explanation.en: After 1921 India entered the second stage of demographic transition.

stem.en: On the eve of independence, the share of the workforce in manufacturing was about:

explanation.en: Agriculture had 70–75%, manufacturing about 10%, services 15–20%.

stem.en: Railways were introduced in India by the British in:

explanation.en: NCERT notes that the British introduced railways in India in 1850.

stem.en: Which of the following regions saw an INCREASE in the share of the workforce in agriculture during the colonial period?

explanation.en: Parts of Madras Presidency, Bombay and Bengal saw a fall in agriculture's share; Orissa, Rajasthan and Punjab saw a rise.

stem.en: Which feature of colonial India's demographic condition does the passage reflect?

options.en: High infant mortality and low life expectancy, with very low literacy
Low birth rate and low death rate

explanation.en: A life expectancy of 32 years and literacy below 16% show poor health and education; birth and death rates were both high.
